explanation: Mathlib has no declaration stating that an idempotent in a local ring is 0 or 1. The only results of this shape are `IsIdempotentElem.iff_eq_zero_or_one` (Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Idempotent.lean), which needs `IsLeftCancelMulZero` (domain-like hypothesis, not available for a general local ring), `equation lemmas`-style `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_bot_or_top` (domains) and `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_bot_or_top_of_isLocalRing` (Noetherian local rings, but about ideals rather than elements). I also grepped `Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/*`, `Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Idempotent.lean`, `Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean` and searched for names like `eq_zero_or_eq_one_of_isIdempotentElem`, `IsIdempotentElem.eq_zero*`, `isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_zero_or_one`, and for `IsLocalRing` lemmas mentioning idempotents; nothing matches. The library's proof combines two Mathlib facts (`IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self` and `IsIdempotentElem.iff_eq_one_of_isUnit`) with case analysis on `1 - e`, i.e. more than a one-or-two-line derivation from a single declaration, so no Mathlib declaration duplicates this result.
